_comment: Takes the MqttCommunication task off Freewheeling on both site
controllers, because a freewheeling task consumes every spare cycle by
definition and that is what stopped the Bijbouw house twice.
WAGO arms a processor-load watchdog in the runtime's own configuration:
[CmpSchedule] ProcessorLoad.Enable=1 / Maximum=95 / Interval=5000
When a 5-second sample of plcload passes 95% the runtime raises
ProcessorLoadWatchdog against App=[all], Task=[all] - it stops everything
and leaves it stopped. Bijbouw's codesyscontrol.log has it twice, on 1 Sep
and 7 Sep 2026, both reading 'plcload=99, maxplcload=95', and nothing in the
six months of log before that.
Measured per thread on Bijbouw (CODESYS names its task threads, so top -H
attributes this directly): MqttCommunication 27.8% instantaneous and ~32%
of the CPU averaged over uptime, against MainTask - the actual house logic,
cyclic 50 ms - at 1.5%. The MQTT task costs twenty times the control logic
because it never sleeps, so the controller sits permanently near the ceiling
and any burst tips one sample over it.
20 ms is not a new number: the task settings already carry Interval=t#20ms,
which CODESYS ignores while the kind is Freewheeling. This makes the kind
match the period that was always declared.
Stal is included even though it has never tripped - same design, same
waste, and it is the control that proved the diagnosis: load average 2.0
against Bijbouw's 3.0-3.6, MQTT thread 13% against 32%, no trips in 7 days
of uptime. Fixing one and not the other would leave the comparison useless
the next time either misbehaves.
Run it against a working copy, never the building's project directly:
./tools/ai/codesys.ps1 scaffold -Project .ai/sync/<Site>/<Site>.project \
-Scaffold tools/ai/scaffold/mqtt-task-cyclic.json -Force
Both tasks already exist, so this updates them. No priority is given: 5 is
correct and stays: below MainTask's 4 so the control logic still preempts
publishing, above RS485's 15 and Ping's 31.
AFTER THE DOWNLOAD, WATCH drop=. A cyclic task drains the publish queue 50
times a second instead of as fast as it can, and the number that says
whether that is enough is DroppedCount, published as drop= in the RS485
BUS_COUNTERS topic every 30 s. It has been 0 throughout; if it starts
climbing on Bijbouw - the Ducobox is the loudest producer on either bus -
the period is too slow and 10 ms is the next step, not a return to
freewheeling.
